6WX1: Ik Oankar = 'Oankar' is taken from the Sanskrit word 'Oan'. This word 'Oan' was used first of all in the Upanishads. In the Mandukya Upanishad it is written that whatever has been, whatever exists at this moment, and whatever will be — this is 'Oan' alone. In the period after the Upanishads the word 'Oan' was used for the collectivity of Vishnu, Shiv and Brahma. The word 'Oankar' occurs in Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji in the sense of 'Akal Purakh', as: Oankari brahma utpati. Oankar kia jini chiti. Oankari sail jug bhae. Oankar bed nirmae. (Ramkali Mahala 1 Dakhani, Oankar). The word 'Ekankar' too (which is the utterance of Ik Oankar) has been used in Sri Guru Granth Sahib, thus: Ekam ekankaru niralaa. Amaru ajoni jati na jala. (Bilavalu Mahala 1 Thiti Gharu 10 Jati). Satinamu: He whose name is 'sati'. The word 'sati' is from the Sanskrit root 'as', whose meaning is 'to be'. The Sanskrit form of 'sati' is 'satya'. Its meaning is 'the one who exists'. The meaning of 'Satinamu' is: 'that One Oankar whose Name is: the One who exists'. There was a king named Sarang. He had three sons. Asraj was by the chief queen; Khan and Sultan were by the other queens. The right to the kingdom was Asraj's. So out of this envy Khan and Sultan both, taking him out on the pretext of a hunt, cut off Asraj's hands and feet and threw him into a well, and said to the father that a lion had killed and eaten Asraj. A band of Vanjaras was passing. One of them went to the well to draw water; he saw Asraj's condition, pity came, he drew him out and treated him, and the wounds healed. As fortune had it, a certain king had died without issue. His ministers had made an agreement that whoever should be met at dawn, and by whose hand the fort's lock should open, he alone was to be made king. At dawn that maimed Asraj was met, and by the touch of his hand alone the lock opened. So he went on ruling there many days; people kept calling him Tundes. One day he was sitting on the roof when those same Vanjaras were passing; seeing them he called them, and having served them and given them wealth, sent them off. The king's officers asked the Vanjaras what their connection with him was. Then the Vanjaras said, we had begun to kill him for some offence, but showing pity we did not kill him — we cut off his hands and feet and left him. This kindness your king has acknowledged. To pronounce the 'h' in the second 'sau' and say 'sahu' is a great error. Those who so pronounce and construe the second 'sau' as 'sahu' construe the word 'nah' as 'not'. This is one further error. H9QC: Sanjog = union, the union of beings. Vijog = separation.
Somewhere there is the union of beings, somewhere separation;
Wonderful is union, and wonderful is separation.
Wonderful is the union and wonderful the separation.
Union and meeting are also of wondrous form; (vijog) separation too is of wondrous form.
GR0R: Somewhere hunger (is tormenting), somewhere there is the enjoyment of things (that is, somewhere many things are being consumed),
Wonderful is hunger, wonderful is satisfaction.
Wonderful is the hunger and wonderful repletion.
Hunger too is of wondrous form; the enjoyments of things are also of wondrous form. Or: seeing the creation of wondrous form, we are left in wonder.
2MP6: Somewhere the praise and laudation (of the Master of creation) is going on,
Wonderful is His Praise, wonderful is His adoration.
Wonderful is Your praise and wonderful Your eulogy.

Those who offer (sifat) praise — the praisers — are also of wondrous form; (salah) laudation too is of wondrous form. Or: by the difference between the speech of Hindus and of Muslims, 'sifat' and 'salah' are two words.
6PMX: Ujharh = the wrong road, having strayed from the true path.
Somewhere there is trackless waste, somewhere there are roads — seeing this wondrous play, astonishment is arising in the mind.
Wonderful is the wilderness, wonderful is the path.
Wonderful is the wilderness and wonderful the path.
The wilderness too is of wondrous form; (rah) the roads too are of wondrous form. Or: the manifest waste and the road are Brahm.
XNJM: (Someone says God is) near, (someone says He is) far;
Wonderful is closeness, wonderful is distance.
Wonderful is Your nearness and wonderful the remoteness from You.
To the knowing He is perceived as near, and that too is of wondrous form; to the ignorant He appears far off, and that too is of wondrous form.
CP34: (Someone says that) pervading all places He is caring for the beings — beholding this wondrous play, a thrill is running through.
How wonderful to behold the Lord, ever-present here.
wonderful is to behold You just present.
Or: in the near and the far, in all, there is wonder upon wonder. Manifestly the Parmeshvar of wondrous form is watching over all. ☬ The creation of Maya:
G06H: Vidan = wondrous play. Vekh = having seen. Rahia vismad = wonder is arising, a trembling is arising in the heart, a shiver is running through the mind.
Seeing (God's) wondrous creation, a kind of shiver is running through the mind.
Beholding His wonders, I am wonder-struck.
Beholding Yours wonders, wonder-struck am I.
Parmeshvar of wondrous form — or, of greatly wondrous form — You are beholding the creation of Maya.
LJUJ: Bujhan = to understand (this 'vidan'). ❀ Note on vismad: In Sanskrit books eight rasas (surges of feeling, waves) of poetry are generally counted (shringar, hasya, karuna, raudra, vir, bhayanak, bibhats and adbhut). But sometimes 'shant ras' is added and nine rasas in all are reckoned. What is the 'adbhut' ras? Astonishment; wonder; vismad. Seeing the countless many-coloured things of nature, an astonishment arises in a person's mind, from which the 'adbhut' ras is produced. Seeing the countless things of nature (seeing which a person's understanding is left bewildered, through which the perfection of the Creator's craftsmanship is made manifest), a kind of trembling, a kind of shiver, comes into a person's mind. This trembling, this shiver, is called 'vismad'. ||1||
O Nanak! This divine spectacle can be understood (only) through great good fortune. ||1||
O Nanak, those who understand this are blessed with perfect destiny. ||1||
Perfectly fortunate are they, O Nanak, who realise this.

Sri Guru Ji says: when there is perfect fortune, then this (bujhan) understanding of the wondrousness comes about. ||1|| ☬ If it be said: this creation of Maya which He is beholding — where is that Maya? To that he says:
HPV2: Kudrat = power, wondrous play, wondrous spectacle. Disai = whatever is being seen. Sukh sar = the essence of comforts.
(O Lord!) Whatever is being seen and whatever is being heard, all this is Your own power; this awe, which is the root of all comforts, is also Your kudrat.
By His Power we see, by His Power we hear; by His Power we have fear, and the essence of happiness.
By Your power we see, by Your power we hear and by your power we fear and have the essence of happiness.
Whatever appears to sight is of the form of Maya, and whatever is heard is also of the form of Maya; and the awe that there is — that is (sukh sar) the most excellent comfort — all that is Maya.
2BTN: Sarab akar = the whole visible form, the whole world.
In the nether regions and in the skies is Your kudrat alone; this whole form (that is, this whole world that is being seen) is Your own wondrous play.
By His Power the nether worlds exist, and the Akaashic ethers; by His Power the entire creation exists.
By Yours power exist the nether regions and skies and by Yours power exists the entire creation.
In the nether regions and the skies there is Maya, and every body is of the form of Maya.
3LQ2: Keteban = the religious books of the Muslims and the Christians. Sarab vichar = all thought, the whole faculty of thought.
The Veds, Puranas and Katebas, (and further) the whole faculty of thought, are Your own power;
By His Power the Vedas and the Puraanas exist, and the Holy Scriptures of the Jewish, Christian and Islamic religions. By His Power all deliberations exist.
By Yours power are the Vedas, the Puranas and the Islamic, Christian and Jewish books, and by Yours power is all deliberation.
The Veds, Purans and (keteba) the Quran that there are — all that is Maya; and all the thought that there is, that too is Maya.
9WJ5: (The beings') eating, drinking and wearing (their whole dealing), and all the love (the impulse of affection) in the world — all this is Your kudrat.
By His Power we eat, drink and dress; by His Power all love exists.
By Your power is eating, drinking and dressing, and by Your power if all love.
Eating, drinking and wearing — this is Maya; and to love in every manner — this too is Maya.
31JA: Jia jahan = among the beings of the world.
Among castes, among kinds, among colours, among the beings of the world, Your kudrat alone is at work,
- By His Power come the species of all kinds and colors; by His Power the living beings of the world exist.
By Yours power are species, kinds and colours, and by Yours, power the living beings of the world.

The distinctions of castes — brahmin and the rest — and kinds of every sort, that is, beasts and birds and the rest, and colours of every sort: all this is Maya alone. And however many beings there are in the world, all that is Maya.
TXG2: (In the world) somewhere deeds of goodness are being done, somewhere there are vices; somewhere someone is being honoured, somewhere pride holds sway — this is Your wondrous play.
By His Power virtues exist, and by His Power vices exist. By His Power come honor and dishonor.
By Yours power are virtues and by yours power the vices. By Yours power are honour and dishonour.
(Nekia) good deeds are Maya, (badia) evil deeds are Maya; man — honour — and (abhiman) dishonour, or pride, whatever there is: all this is Maya.
R5T7: Air, water, fire, the dust of the earth (and the other elements) — all these are Your spectacle alone.
By His Power wind, water and fire exist; by His Power earth and dust exist.
By Your power are wind, water and fire and by Your power are the earth and dust.
Air, water and fire — all these are of the form of Maya; and the earth, which is of the form of dust, is (kudrat) Maya.
TJUE: Paki = pure. Nai = greatness, praise. Pak = (You Yourself are) pure.
(O Lord!) All Your power is at work; You are the master of kudrat, You alone are the maker of this play; Your greatness is the purest of the pure, You Yourself are (of a) pure (being).
Everything is in Your Power, Lord; You are the all-powerful Creator. Your Name is the Holiest of the Holy.
Everything, is Your might. You t the Omnipotent Creator, and Your Name is the holiest of the holy.
O Creator Being, maker of all! All is Your Maya; You Yourself are pure, and Your (nai) greatness too is pure.
ZU0T: Vekhai = He cares for. Tako tak = alone, Himself by Himself. Vartai = is at work, is present. ||2||
O Nanak! The Lord, (keeping this whole kudrat) within His own command, is caring for (all), and (everywhere, alone) He Himself is present. ||2||
O Nanak, through the Command of His Will, He beholds and pervades the creation; He is absolutely unrivalled. ||2||
Says Nanak, through Your pleasure, You O Lord beholdest and pervadest everything Altogether unrivalled You are.

Sri Guru Ji says: keeping all within Your own command, You are watching over all, and (tako tak) the One alone is at work. Or: O Shaikh Brahm! Behold (tak) that One who is at work. ||2|| ☬ Question: earlier, in the second pauri, Dharam Rai was called the taker of the account; then it is said 'behold the One' — how are these two arranged together? ☬ Answer:
EGUF: Bhog = the enjoyment of things. Bhog kai = having enjoyed, having used. Hoi = having become. Bhasmar = a mound of ashes, a heap of dust. Bhaur = the soul. Vada hoa = died.

God Himself (having become the form of the being) enjoys the colours of the things (this too is His wondrous kudrat). (The body) becomes a heap of dust (and at last the soul-form) bhaur sets off (leaving the body).
Enjoying his pleasures, one is reduced to a pile of ashes, and the soul passes away.
Enjoying revelments, man himself becomes a heap of ashes and his soul passes away.
The beings themselves have taken their enjoyments. When one died, then out of this (bhasmar) body that had turned to ash the delusion-form being went away.
TD8H: Dunidar = a worldly man, a being entangled in the world. Gal = around the neck. Ghat = having put. Chalaia = driven on ahead.

(When) a being of this kind, caught in the affairs of the world, dies, a chain is put around (its) neck and it is driven on ahead (that is, a being wrapped up in Maya does not wish to leave the world, and 'hans chalsi dumana').
He may be great, but when he dies, the chain is thrown around his neck, and he is led away.
When the worldly man dies, a chain is thrown around his neck and he is led away.
However great a worldly man he had become, just so great and heavy a chain the messengers of death put around his neck and drove him on ahead.
XM1T: Agai = in the world beyond. Karni = the earnings of one's deeds. Kirat = greatness, praise and laudation. Vachiai = is read out, is counted in the reckoning. Bah = having sat down, that is, with patience and thoroughly.

In the world beyond (that is, in Dharam Raj's court — see pauri 2) only the earnings in the form of God's praise and laudation are accepted; there the account (of the being's deeds) is thoroughly explained (to it).
There, his good and bad deeds are added up; sitting there, his account is read.
There, his good and bad acts are read out to this and seating Him his account to explained to him.

When he went on ahead into the world beyond, before Dharam Rai, then according to his deeds his (kirat) renown, or his ill-repute, is read out — that is, Chitr and Gupt read out and recite his good and his evil. And Dharam Rai, seating him down, made up the account and explained: this is the fruit of your deeds that you will receive.
W315: Thau na hovi = no shelter is found. Paudii = while blows are falling, while the shoes are falling. Hun = at this time, when the beating falls. Kia ruaia = which cry, which weeping, which entreaty. Suniai = is heard.
(Because of having stayed entangled only in the enjoyments of Maya) no shelter is found there for the one on whom the blows are falling; at that time not one of its cries and entreaties is heard.
He is whipped, but finds no place of rest, and no one hears his cries of pain.
When thrashed, he finds no place of shelter, but none hears his bewailing now.
Blows fall upon the evil-doers; then no place is found to escape them. When they begin to weep, then the messengers of death say: what will your weeping be heard for now — that is, no one hears it.
LLCH: Man = the mind. Andhai = the blind one. Gavaia = wasted. ||3||
The (being) of foolish mind wastes its own (human) birth for nothing. ||3||
The blind man has wasted his life away. ||3||
The blind man has wasted away his life.

O being of blind mind! You have wasted your human birth — that is, you have ruined it. Now that it is done, what do you weep for? ||3|| ☬ He now states the salok that gives the meaning of the hearing of the Ved:
W3RM: Bhai vich = in fear. Pavan vahai = the wind blows. Sadvau = sada-ev, always.
The wind is always blowing in God's fear.
In the Fear of God, the wind and breezes ever blow.
In Lord's fear wind and breeze ever blow.
The wind that has (sad) a good course, or (pavan) the gale, (sadvau) the most excellent wind — that is, the one that is cool, soft and fragrant.
D11B: Lakhs of rivers too are flowing in that fear alone.
In the Fear of God, thousands of rivers flow.
In Lord's fear flow lacs of rivers.
This blows in the fear of Akal Purakh, and lakhs of (dariau) rivers too move in that fear.
LF00: The fire that is performing service — this too is in God's fear alone.
In the Fear of God, fire is forced to labor.
In Lord's fear fire is forced to perform labour.
The fire performs the forced labour of all beings in fear — that is, it accomplishes the work of all.
CW8D: Bhar = under the weight. Ind = the god Indra, the cloud.
The whole earth is pressed down under its weight only because of God's fear.
In the Fear of God, the earth is crushed under its burden.
In Lord's fear the earth is trampled under burden.
Through fear the earth is pressed down by (bhar) its burden.
QU0B: Firai = moves. Sir bhar = on its head.
In God's fear King Indra is moving on his head (that is, the clouds are flying in His will alone).
In the Fear of God, the clouds move across the sky.
In Lord's fear the cloud moves head-long.
On its head — that is, applying its whole force — Indra the cloud, or Indra himself, moves through fear in the business of his rule.
3AG6: Raja dharam duar = the door of Dharam Raja.
Dharam Raj's court too is in God's fear.
In the Fear of God, the Righteous Judge of Dharma stands at His Door.
In Lord's fear Dharamraj (righteous Judge) stands at His door.
Dharam Raja too, seated at his own door, or at the door of Parmeshvar, delivers judgement in that fear.
SXZD: The sun too and the moon too are in God's command,
In the Fear of God, the sun shines, and in the Fear of God, the moon reflects.
In Lord's fear is retrained the sun and in Lord's fear the moon.
In fear the sun, in fear the moon.
7LTR: Travelling crores of kos, the end of the journey does not come.
They travel millions of miles, endlessly.
They travel myriads of miles without an end.
They travel crores of kos; the end does not come.
A7J0: Sidh = those great souls who had attained the eight siddhis, anima and the rest, were called siddhs; accomplished yogis. Budh = the wise, those who are free from the world's bonds of Maya.
Siddhs, Budhs, gods and Naths — all are in God's fear.
In the Fear of God, the Siddhas exist, as do the Buddhas, the demi-gods and Yogis.
In Lord's fear are the men of miracles, Bhudhas, the demigods and the Yogis.
However many siddhs there are, those who are wise, or Budh and the rest, the nine planets that there are, and the nine gods, and the Naths — all are in fear.
2WFN: These skies stretched out above (which are seen — these too) are in that fear alone.
In the Fear of God, the Akaashic ethers are stretched across the sky.
In Lord's fear is stretched the sky.
The sky too is (adane) spread out, or without support; that too is in fear.
QXCX: Warriors and heroes of very great strength are all in God's fear.
In the Fear of God, the warriors and the most powerful heroes exist.
In Lord's fear are the warriors and the very powerful heroes.
The great warriors, the strong, who are heroes — or the rathi, the maharathi and the atirathi — are also in fear.
KUE7: Aveh = (whatever beings) come (into the world). Pur = all the beings entire, who are seated in the boat of life in this world-ocean.
Boatloads upon boatloads of beings, who are born and die in the world, are all in that fear.
In the Fear of God, multitudes come and go.
In Lord's fear multitudes come and go.
Boatloads upon boatloads all come and go in fear — that is, they are born and they die.
ARLE: Sagalia sir = upon the heads of all beings. Lekh likhia = the writ in the form of fear is written.
On the foreheads of all beings the writ in the form of fear is written — that is, the Lord's law is just this, that all are in His fear.
God has inscribed the Inscription of His Fear upon the heads of all.
The Lord has written the writ of His fear on the heads of all.
On the heads of all beings the writ of fear is written.
QHW8: O Nanak! Only the one true Nirankar is free of fear. ||1||
O Nanak, the Fearless Lord, the Formless Lord, the True Lord, is One. ||1||
Nanak, the True Formless Lord alone is fearless.
Sri Guru Ji says: free of fear is the one truth-form Nirankar. ||1|| ☬ Confirming the meaning stated in the previous salok, he shows the world's impermanence by telling of its strangeness:
ECUL: Hor = all the others (apart from Nirankar). Raval = dust, (that is) trifling.
O Nanak! The one Nirankar alone is free of fear; many others like (the incarnate) Ram (Ji) are trifling (before that Nirankar);
O Nanak, the Lord is fearless and formless; myriads of others, like Rama, are mere dust before Him.
Nanak the Formless Lord alone is fearless, and many others like Ram are as dust before Him.

Sri Guru Ji says: the fearless Nirankar is indeed Ram; other beings are many, of the form of (raval) dust. Or: the other incarnations, Ram and the rest, are of the line of Parmeshvar's hair-tips, or are workers of ramal.
33GA: Ketia = how many; countless. Kanh kahania = the tales of Krishna Ji.
(Against the knowledge of that Nirankar) the many tales of Krishna (Ji) and the many reflections of the Veds are also trifling.
There are so many stories of Krishna, so many who reflect over the Vedas.
Good many are the stories of Krishan and good many the reciters of Vedas.

(Kanh) the tales of Krishna are many; those who tell the tales are many — that is, they are numerous. And how many Veds there are, and how many there are who reflect on the Ved — that is, the tellers too are many.
B11F: Gir mur = whirling and turning, returning again and again.
(In order to obtain the knowledge of that Nirankar) many people become beggars and dance, and keep many kinds of rhythm,
So many beggars dance, spinning around to the beat.
Many a beggar dance and, turning and bending round, beat the time.
And how many beggars dance; (gir mur pureh tal) turning again and again, with gestures and expressions, they keep the rhythm.
7NHM: Bajari = players of ras. Ai kadheh bajar = they come and perform ras plays.
The ras-players too come into the bazaars and perform their plays,
The magicians perform their magic in the market place, creating a false illusion.
The guisers come in the market place and exhibit a false show.

(Bajari) the jesters — that is, the actors who perform plays, the nats, or the ras-players — coming into the bazaar bring out the apparatus of the spectacle, and sit with their own (bajar) shop opened.
7WZH: Al = trick, deceit. Al patal = the tricks of the nether world, words of very deep trickery, words that others do not understand.
Taking on the forms of kings and queens they sing, and (from their mouths) they speak words of many kinds,
They sing as kings and queens, and speak of this and that.
They sing as King and queens and speak of the upper and the lower regions.
They sing the episodes of kings and queens; (al patal) they talk of sky and nether world, or they talk in a disordered way.
DUH0: They wear earrings and necklaces worth lakhs of rupees (that is, costly ones);
They wear earrings, and necklaces worth thousands of dollars.
They wear ear-rings worth lacs of rupees and necklace worth lakhs.

So in the dance of those bazaar-players they act the parts of those who wear (mundre) earrings, or rings, worth a lakh of (takia) rupees, and necklaces worth lakhs of rupees; or they wear them themselves.
LHBA: Jit tan = on whichever body. Paiah = are worn.

But, O Nanak! (Those poor people do not know that these earrings and necklaces —) whichever bodies they are put upon, those bodies (in the end) become ashes (and by this singing and dancing, by the wearing of these earrings and necklaces, how can 'knowledge' be obtained?)
Those bodies on which they are worn, O Nanak, those bodies turn to ashes.
The bodies on which they are worn, O Nanak, those bodies becomes ashes.

Sri Guru Ji says: the body on which necklaces and other ornaments are worn — that body turns to ashes. ☬ If it be said: those who in the ras become the form of Narad and utter such knowledge as 'aham brahmasmi' — how will their destruction come about? Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji says: those who merely talk of knowledge and make themselves out to be fearless — to that he says:

H9ZU: Galii = by way of talk. Kathna = to describe. Sar = iron.
Knowledge cannot be sought out by mere talk; (to describe how knowledge can be obtained) is as hard as iron (that is, it is very difficult).
Wisdom cannot be found through mere words. To explain it is as hard as iron.
Divine Knowledge is not sought by mere worlds. To explain it is hard like iron.

As for uttering knowledge by way of talk — (dhudhiai), that is, if we consider and look, there is no knowledge in them. To utter knowledge while holding to it — this is (karra) difficult; and the fruit of knowledge is (sar) the most excellent, that is, kaivalya.
J35Q: Karam = by (the Lord's) grace. Hikmat = cleverness, device. ||2||
(Yes) if it is given by God's mercy then it is obtained; (without that mercy any) other contrivance, or the exercising of command, is useless. ||2||
When the Lord bestows His Grace, then alone it is received; other tricks and orders are useless. ||2||
If one becomes the recipient of Lord's grace, then alone he obtains it. Other devices and orders are ruinous.

So such knowledge is obtained if the grace of Akal Purakh is received; and by (hikmat) contrivance and (hukam) the giving of orders the being is made khuar — that is, it comes to ruin. ||2|| ☬ If it be asked: how then is one saved from ruin? To that he says:
ZZTA: Nadar = the glance of grace. Kareh = (O Lord! You) cast. Nadri = by Your glance of grace.
O Lord! If You cast Your glance of grace (upon a being), then by Your gracious sight it obtains the Satguru.
If the Merciful Lord shows His Mercy, then the True Guru is found.
If the merciful Master shows His mercy, then, is the True Guru obtained.
If Hari casts His own glance of grace, then (nadri) the one who looks with grace — that is, the protecting Satguru — is obtained.
LESG: Bharammia = has wandered. Satgur = the Satguru.
(When) this (poor) being had wandered through many births (and Your glance of grace came), then the Satguru recited His shabad to it.
This soul wandered through countless incarnations, until the True Guru instructed it in the Word of the Shabad.
This soul wandered through many births and then, the True Guru communicated to it the Name.
This being has come wandering through many births. When grace came, then the Satgurus recited the (sabad) teaching.
DBKA: Sabh lok sabaia = O all you people!
O all you people! Listen attentively: there is no other giver equal to the Satguru.
There is no giver as great as the True Guru; hear this, all you people.
There is no benefactor so great as the True Guru, Hear this, all, O you people.

There is no giver equal to the Satgurus. Whoever has come into the assembly — let all people hear this thing. Or: whoever has come into the world, all who die without having heard the Guru's teaching, or who have come into (bavan) crookedness.
T8FJ: Satgur miliai = if the Satguru is met (which Satguru? Answer: 'jin sacho sach bujhaia'). Sach = the ever-abiding Lord. Jinhi = those people who. Ap = one's own self, self-regard, ego.
Those people who have driven out self-regard from within themselves obtained the true Lord by the meeting of that Satguru,
Meeting the True Guru, the True Lord is found; He removes self-conceit from within,
By meeting the Satguru, who has removed self-conceit from within him,
By (miliai) meeting the Satguru, truth is obtained; or, it is they who have obtained it.
765B: Sacho sach = utter truth, truth alone. Bujhaia = made to understand. Jin = which (Guru). ||4||

the Satguru who has given the understanding of the utterly true Lord. (That is, those people who drive out self-regard from within themselves obtain the true God by the meeting of that Satguru who gives the understanding of the ever-abiding Lord.) ||4||
and instructs us in the Truth of Truths. ||4||
and who preaches all truth, attains the True Lord.

Those who have removed self-regard from within, and again those to whom the Satgurus have declared truth upon truth — they have lost their pride. ||4|| ☬ At one time, somewhere, ras-players performed a ras. Then the Sikhs said, let us go and see the ras. To that, Guru Ji, showing the materials of the true ras that concerns Parmeshvar, says:
60GC: Gharia = just as the Punjabi word 'ghara' comes from the Sanskrit 'ghat', and just as Punjabi 'kara' comes from the Sanskrit 'katak', so Punjabi 'ghari' comes from the Sanskrit 'ghatika'. 'Ghari' is the name of a division of time, equal to 24 minutes. Gopi = a keeper of cows, a Gujar woman. This word 'gopi' is used especially for the Gujar women of Bindraban, who used to play with Krishna Ji during his stay at Gokul. Krishna Ji was born in Mathura, which according to the Hindu faith is one of the seven most sacred cities of India. Those seven cities are: Ajudhia, Mathura, Maya, Kansi, Kanchi, Avantika and Puri. Pahar = an eighth part of the whole day, equal to 3 hours. Kanh = the Prakrit form of the Sanskrit word 'Krishna'. Gopal = a name of Krishna Ji.
(All) the gharis are (as it were) gopis; (all) the pahars (of the day) are (as it were) Kanh;
All the hours are the milk-maids, and the quarters of the day are the Krishnas.
All the hours are milk-maids and the quarters of a day are Krishans and herds-men.
He describes the form of the ras: the (gharia) ghatikas of day and night are the gopis; the eight pahars that there are, these are the (gopal) cowherd boys along with (kanh) Krishna.
0VSR: Air, water and fire are (as it were) ornaments (which those gopis have put on). (In the ras plays the ras-players sing, making up the mimicry of the incarnations; in the ras of nature) the moon and the sun are (as it were) two incarnations.
The wind, water and fire are the ornaments; the sun and moon are the incarnations.
The wind, water and the fire are the ornaments and the moon and the sun are the incarnations.

Air, water and fire — these three are the ornaments of the gopis in the form of the gharis of the four-month seasons: Savan, Bhadon, Asu, Katik — in these four months water is the ornament; Maghar, Poh, Magh, Phagan — in these fire is the ornament; Chet, Visakh, Jeth, Asarh — in these air is the ornament. In this, the moon and the sun are the incarnations Ram and Krishna, whose play is going on.
MWZG: The whole earth is the goods and wealth (for the performing of the ras), and (the affairs of the world) are the ras's properties and paraphernalia.
All of the earth, property, wealth and articles are all entanglements.
All the goods of the earth, property, wealth and other things of use, are all entanglements

However much earth there is, this is the wealth and goods — cows and the rest — in this ras; and whatever is going on in the world, all that is of the form of entanglement. He now makes this same point clear:
RS8R: Musai = is being cheated. Vihuni = empty, void. ||1||
(In this ras of Maya) the world, void of knowledge, is being cheated, and Jamkal is devouring it. ||1||

The disciples, the bhagtias, (vain) play the instruments; (gur) Ram and Krishna dance.

They move their feet and roll their heads.

For the sake of bread they beat out the rhythm.

and they dash themselves upon the ground.

The Lord is fearless and formless; His Name is True.
Fearless is the Formless Lord, whose Name is true,
He whose Name is true — He is Nirankar, He is free of fear.

The entire universe is His Creation.
and whose creation is the whole world.
He whose making this whole world is.

Only those servants remember Him within whom, by (God's) grace, there is that ascendant state, those in whose mind there is the eagerness (to remember Him),

Those upon whom there is the rising of Akal Purakh's (karam) grace — they, becoming servants, perform His service.

the life-night of those servants passes sweetly —

Dewy (cool) is the night of those within whose mind is the Lord's love.
Those in whose mind there is love, their night in the form of their state is (bhinni) drenched, or made tender, by the bliss of the soul.

Those who have learnt this teaching through the Guru's wisdom,
Contemplating the Guru, I have been taught these teachings;

Those who have learnt from the Gurus the teaching for the attaining of Vahiguru — that is, have taken it — to them reflection has come through the Gurus.

granting His Grace, He carries His servants across.
that the Merciful Master, through His mercy, ferries His slave across.

(Nadri) Vahiguru, by His own (karam) grace, carries them across the world-ocean. ☬ If it be said: those who dance in the Krishna and Ram lila — will they gain some merit or not? He now condemns their dancing that is without love:

the countless whirlwinds of the deserts,

and many and endless, desert, whirl--winds,

spinning tops, churning staffs, threshing boards,

the breathless tumblings of the birds,
the breathless tumblings of the birds,

and the men moving round and round on spindles

Nanak, the tumblers are countless and endless.

0LF9: Bandhan bandh = having bound them in bonds.

According to the acts performed, every one dances.
Being subject each to their own performed deeds, all dance.

Those who dance and dance and laugh, then at the time of departing they weep.

4270: Dancing and leaping is (only) an enthusiasm of the mind,

Dancing and leaping is an enthusiasm of the mind; by this, love does not come about.

Nanak, those who have God's fear in their mind, in their mind is His love as well.

UKTR: Nai laiai = if (Your) Name is remembered.

O brother! The Name of Nirankar brings about your welfare; by repeating the Name one does not go into hell.
UC30: Pind = the body. Tis da = of that (God). Khaje = food, sustenance, nourishment.

Knowing (jiu pind) the body to be that Akal Purakh's, (de) giving according to one's capacity, let us (khajai) take food. (Akh gavaiai) it is lost by the telling. Or: what one is to say with the mouth, that 'I gave' — let us lose that, that is, let us not say it.

If you desirest your good, O man, perform virtuous deeds and feel lowly.
If you wish your own good, then having done meritorious deeds, have yourself called (nich) lowly.

If you remove the signs of old-age, the old age shall come to you in guise (of death etc.)

If by yogic practice and the like (jarvana) death has been driven off, still it does not retreat; or, if one should cast off (jarvana) old age, drive it away, still it does not come about — on the contrary, old age comes on, taking on its disguise.

The Muslims, reading and reading their own book of religion, have made (sifat) its praise; and reading and reading they reflect upon that same sharia.

Parmeshvar, who is worthy of it — the Hindus praise Him; and to them comes the sight of that boundless form.

The Yogis, that there are, meditate on the Absolute Lord and name the Creator as Unseen.

In the mind of the generous, contentment is produced and they think of giving (in charity)
Those who are satis, speakers of truth, in their minds the qualities of truth and contentment and the rest arise. Those who are givers, in their minds the thought of giving arises.

Having given and given, they ask of the Lord a thousandfold for their charity. In the Hindus' doctrine a thousandfold is written; among the Muslims seventyfold is written.

The thieves, adulterers, perjurers, evil-doers and sinners
The thieves, adulterers, perjurers evil-doers and sinners.

Those who (by doing vice after vice) use up the earnings made in the past and set off (from here empty-handed) — (but these are the Kartar's own colours) to them too (He Himself) has entrusted some such task.
- after using up what good karma they had, they depart; have they done any good deeds here at all?

Some have at hand — that is, the merit that (hoda) was made in a former birth — and having (khai) enjoyed it in this world they then go off to the hells. JAEC: Jal = in the water. Jia = beings. Loa = worlds. Akara akar = of all the visible universes.

There are beings and creatures in the water and on the land, in the worlds and universes, form upon form.
There are beings in water, on land, in the worlds, in the universes and in the worlds, in the germs and microbes.

However many hosts of beings there are in the waters and on the lands; whatever living things there are in the realms of Barun and Indra and the rest, in the fourteen worlds; and again, whatever (akar) bodies there are within bodies — that is, lice and the like.
U97T: Oi = all those beings. Ji = whatever. Tun hai = You alone, (O Lord!). Sar = strength, power, support.

What they say, that you knowest and for them, too, You carest.
How far shall I tell? What they say — O Akal Purakh! You alone know it. (Bhi) again, (tina bhi) their (sar) news is in Your (sar) keeping.
HNGA: Bhukh salahan = the hunger in the form of praise and laudation. Adhar = support.

O Nanak, the hunger of the devotees is to praise You; the True Name is their only support.

Sri Guru Ji says: those who are Your devotees — to them there remains only the (bhukh) longing for Your praise; and, O Truth-form! the support of Your Name remains to them.
TVY1: Pa chhar = the dust of the feet. ||1||

The clay of a Muslim (in the grave after death) falls into the potter's clod.

DP7H: Kia = made. Kare pukar = (that clay, as it were) makes an outcry.

Then, placing it on the wheel, they shape vessels of that very clay, and bricks too are made. Then, stacking them in the kiln, they set fire to them. GT2R: Jal jal = burning and burning. Paveh = they fall (to the ground).
Burning, the poor thing weeps, and embers fall and fall from it,
The poor clay burns, burns and weeps, as the fiery coals fall upon it.
The poor clay burns, burns and weeps and the fiery coals continually fall from to it.
That poor clay of the Muslims weeps, burning and burning, and embers of fire fall and fall from upon it.

J8C9: Rakhion = He has placed (to understand this verb form, see 'Gurbani Viakaran').

DJNC: Satgur miliai = if (such) a Guru is met.

Meeting the True Guru, eternal liberation is obtained; He has banished attachment from within.
Salvation is obtained for aye, by meeting the True Guru, who has banished worldly attachment from within him.
By the meeting with the Satgurus a person becomes forever of the form of the liberated. And he has become so who has driven out attachment from within his heart — that is, has removed it.
EZ5K: (Above all other cleverness) this reflection is the fine one: that the person who has joined his mind to his Guru,
This is the highest thought, that one's consciousness is attached to the True Lord.
The excellent idea (theme) is this that one attaches one's mind to the True Lord.
This excellent reflection is obtained by the one who has joined his mind to the true Parmatma.
USJC: Jag jivan = the life of the world, the very life of the world (the Lord). ❀ Note: to take 'paio' and 'paia' to mean 'obtained in past time' and 'obtained now' is incorrect according to grammar. he has obtained the Life of the World, the Giver. ||6||

In pride man comes, in pride he departs.
Coming and going come about through pride.
2BJR: sometimes it is born, sometimes it dies.
In ego they are born, and in ego they die.
In pride he is born, in pride he dies.
Being born and dying come about through pride.
ZZ9C: Remaining within the boundary of this separate existence, the being sometimes gives (to some needy person) and sometimes takes (from someone, to fulfil its own need).
In ego they give, and in ego they take.
In pride he gives, in pride he takes.
Giving and taking come about through pride.
9C0F: In this very notion of 'I, I' (that 'I' do this work, 'I' do it) it sometimes earns and sometimes loses.
In ego they earn, and in ego they lose.
In pride he earns, in pride he losses.
Earning and losing come about through pride.
R989: As long as the being is within the boundary of mine-and-yours, it is (in people's eyes) sometimes truthful, sometimes false.
In ego they become truthful or false.
In pride he becomes true or false.
Being truthful and being false come about through pride.
0F2V: As long as it is in the delusion of an existence separate from its Creator, so long it goes on counting the tally of its own sins and merits (that is, it thinks: 'I' have done these good deeds, 'I' have done these bad deeds),

In pride he reflects on virtue or vice.
The reckoning of sin and the reckoning of merit come about through pride.
Y5P1: Narak surag avtar = falling into hell or into heaven.
and because of remaining in this very separateness (that is, through not making its own self one with God) it sometimes falls into hell, sometimes into heaven.

In pride he falls in hell or heaven.
Being born (avtar) in hell and being born in heaven come about through pride.
SGDK: As long as the being is bound in an existence separate from its Kartar, so long it sometimes laughs and sometimes weeps (that is, sometimes it thinks itself happy, sometimes miserable).
In ego they laugh, and in ego they weep.
In pride he laughs, in pride he weeps.
Laughing and weeping come about through pride.
SJ9B: Bhariai = it becomes soiled (with the filth of sins).

In ego they become dirty, and in ego they are washed clean.
In pride he is soiled, in pride he is washed off.

Being foolish and being clever come about through pride.

He knows not the worth of salvation and emancipation.
The not knowing of the (sar) secret of (mokh mukat) kaivalya liberation.

Maya in which pure sattva predominates; ignorance in which tamas predominates, the shadow; or the working of the shadow of deceit — all such things come about through pride.

Living in ego, mortal beings are created.
By taking pride the beings are created.
However much begetting of beings there is, all of it is through pride.

Nanak, by Lord's order the destiny is recorded.

The (jat) origin of haumai is just this: that deeds are done through haumai.

This is the bondage of ego, that time and time again, they are reborn.

So this very haumai is the giver of bonds, and through this the beings fall into births again and again.

(Of itself the question arises in the mind: from where is this delusion of a separate existence born, and by what method can it be removed?)
Where does ego come from? How can it be removed?
Where is ego born from and by what way is it removed?
So from where is the arising of haumai, and in what manner does haumai depart?

This ego exists by the Lord's Order; people wander according to their past actions.
This is the Lord's will that on account of ego men wander according to their past acts.
Now he states the conclusion: this haumai too is from the command alone; and as the deed has fallen, that is, has been written, according to that it makes the beings wander.

You are the Great Forgiver; You give continually, more and more each day.

You who are (agla) the giver of much bounty, or who from beginningless time give gifts daily to the beings, and it increases the more — that is, nothing of Yours grows less.

Human beings, trees, pilgrimage places, banks (that is, rivers), clouds, fields,
Men, trees, sacred shrines of pilgrimage, banks of sacred rivers, clouds, fields,
Men, trees, holy places, banks of sacred streams, clouds and fields,
Among persons, among trees, of the pilgrimage places, among the banks, among the clouds, among the fields.

islands, worlds, spheres, regions, universes, lakes, and mountains such as Meru,
islands, continents, worlds, solar systems, and universes;
islands, spheres, universes, continents and solar systems,

the creatures of the four sources of origin (andaj, jeraj, utbhuj, setaj) —
the four sources of creation - born of eggs, born of the womb, born of the earth and born of sweat;
the sources of creation, egg-born, womb-born, earth-born and sweat-born,

the reckoning of the number of all these is known by that Lord alone (who has created them all).

and oceans, mountains and sentient beings; He, the Lord, knows their condition,

O Nanak, without the True Name, of what use is the frontal mark of the Hindus, or their sacred thread? ||1||
Nanak, without the True Name, of what avail is frontal mark and of what a sacred thread?

lacs of Divine comprehensions and concentrations and lacs of readings of Vedas and recitations of Puranas,

Truth is obtained by meeting the True Guru, in whose mind the truth abides.
Those Satgurus in whose hearts You have settled truth — O Truth-form! You are obtained through the meeting with those Satgurus.

no benefit of taking birth in the world comes to them. ||8||

Why have they (such persons) come into the world?

The more one writes and reads, the more one burns.

He who goes bare footed, obtains the fruit of his actions.
He remains (upetana) bare of foot; he does not wear sandals. As the fruit of the sin he has committed in the past, thorns prick his feet.
LJU1: Al mal = filthy things. Sir = on the head. Chhai = ashes.
(Abandoning pure and good food) he eats what is foul, and has put ashes on his head,
One who eats filth and throws ashes on his head
He, who eats fifth and throws ashes on his head.
Practising the discipline of the left-hand path, he has taken to eating dung and urine; he has become an aghori, he has put ash on his head.
T8LZ: Murakh = the fool. Pat = honour. Thai na pai = it does not find a place, it is not accepted.
The ignorant fool has (in this way) lost his own honour.
the blind fool loses his honor.
He the blind fool, loses his honour.
This blind and foolish being, being without the Name, has lost his honour indeed.
R5ZK: Apart from the Lord's Name no other effort is accepted.
Without the Name, nothing is of any use.
Without the Name, nothing becomes acceptable.
Without the Name no deed comes (thai) to its place — that is, none of it bears fruit.
ZVGP: He goes and lives in the wastes, among the tombs, among the cremation grounds,
One who lives in the wilderness, in cemetaries and cremation grounds
He who dwells in wilderness and at burial and cremation-ground.
He lives in (bebani) the wastes; he lives among the tombs and the cremation grounds.
BCWR: Andh = the blind, the foolish person.
The blind (fool) does not understand (the way of God), and repents when the time has passed.
- that blind man does not know the Lord; he regrets and repents in the end.
That blind man knows not the Lord and regrets afterwards.
Through the holding of these hypocrisies the blind being does not know Parmeshvar; then at the end the understanding of the blind and ignorant one makes its repentance.

PAPD: Satgur bhete = (the person to whom) the Guru is met.
The person to whom the Guru is met, he alone enjoys (true) happiness,
One who meets the True Guru finds peace.
He who meets the True Guru, attains peace.
Those who meet the Satgurus, they obtain happiness.
1P09: He (the very fortunate one) settles God's Name within his heart.
He enshrines the Name of the Lord in his mind.
God's name, he implants in his mind.
He settles the Name of Hari within his mind.
9WJN: (But) O Nanak! The Guru too is met only by the one on whom the Giver Himself casts His glance of grace.
O Nanak, when the Lord grants His Grace, He is obtained.
Nanak he to whom the Lord shows mercy attains Him.
He upon whom Akal Purakh casts the glance of grace, he obtains the Satgurus.
BJLC: Andese = anxiety. Te = from. Nihkeval = untouched, unstained. Sabad = through the shabad. ||2||
Becoming unstained by the world's hopes and anxieties, he burns away his own haumai through the Guru's shabad. ||2||
He becomes free of hope and fear, and burns away his ego with the Word of the Shabad. ||2||
From hope and fear, he becomes free and his ego, he burns with God's Name.
Becoming free of hope and (andese) doubt and all such things, burning away the sense of 'I' and 'mine' in the Guru's shabad, the gurmukh becomes pure. ||2||
JY3A: Terai man = in Your mind. Dar = at (Your) door. Kirat = renown, greatness.
(O Lord!) The devotees are dear to You in Your own mind, who are singing Your praise and laudation and are resplendent at Your door.
Your devotees are pleasing to Your Mind, Lord. They look beautiful at Your door, singing Your Praises.
The Saints, O Lord, are pleasing to Your mind, They look beautiful and sing Yours praises at Your gate.
Those devotees who at the door of Your holy congregation are resplendent, singing Your kirtan — they (bhavde) seem good in Your mind.
CHF5: Karma bahre = the ill-fated. Dhoa = support. Dhavde = they wander about.
O Nanak! The ill-fated people wander about; they find no place at the Lord's door,
O Nanak, those who are denied Your Grace, find no shelter at Your Door; they continue wandering.
Nanak, they who are destitute of Your favour find not shelter at Yours door and wander about.

Those who are outside good deeds — that is, who have not performed desireless deeds and the company of the holy — they do not (dhoa na lahni) take hold of support at the door of Your holy congregation, or they find no honour; they (dhavde) run about through the eighty-four.
BN22: Ik = many beings. Mul = the root, the Lord. Anhoda = without having the thing (in the house) at all. Ap = one's own self. Ganaide = they make themselves out to be great.
(Because) these (poor) ones do not understand their own essence; without having (the capital of divine quality within them) at all, they make themselves out to be great.
Some do not understand their origins, and without cause, they display their self-conceit.
Some know not origin and without cause exhibit their self-conceit.
Some manmukhs do not know their own root, which is Brahm; they count themselves, without having it at all, in the pride of body and caste.
84WZ: Hau = I. Dhadhi = one who praises, one who sings the var, a bard. Dhadhi ka = a poor little bard (as ghatuka = a little pot). Nich jat = of a low caste. Hor = other people. Utam jat = of high caste.
(O Lord!) I am a poor little bard of low caste (at Your door); other people call themselves of high caste.
I am the Lord's minstrel, of low social status; others call themselves high caste.
I am the Lord's bard of low birth, others call themselves of high caste.
And Bias and Vasisht and the rest are called of high caste; I am Your (dhadhi) singer of praise, of (nich) low caste.
35QW: I beg (Your 'Name') from those who perform Your worship. ||9||
I seek those who meditate on You. ||9||
I ask for the society of those, who meditate on You.
From those who perform Your meditation I beg Your Name; or, from those who meditate on You I beg their company. ||9|| ☬ He shows the falsity of the world:
2M3H: Kur = deceit, delusion (Note: the word 'kur' is not an adjective, it is a 'noun', and is masculine. This is the very reason that even with feminine words such as 'marhi', 'kaia', 'bibi', the word 'kur' remains masculine singular).

This whole world is of the form of deceit (as the whole show of a conjuror is of the form of deceit); (in it someone is) a king (and many people are) subjects. These too are only deceit (like the conjuror's showing of coins and shells).
False is the king, false are the subjects; false is the whole world.
False is the King, false the subjects and false is the entire world.
The king and the subjects that there are in the world — all of them are of the form of falsehood.
BMMK: Mandap = canopies. Marhi = palace. Baisanhar = the one who dwells (in the palace).
(In this world somewhere there are these kings') canopies and palaces and mansions (these) too are of the form of deceit, and the one who dwells in them (the king) is deceit as well.
False is the mansion, false are the skyscrapers; false are those who live in them.
False is the mansion, false the sky-scraper and false is the dweller therein.
(Mandap) the place, (marhi) the mansion, and those who sit within them — all are of the form of falsehood.
YGJA: Gold and silver (and those who wear gold and silver too) are only of the form of delusion,
False is gold, and false is silver; false are those who wear them.
False is gold, false is silver and false is the wearer.
Gold and silver, and those who make their disciplines of them, are all of the form of falsehood.
HNWX: Kaia = the body. Apar = boundless, very much.
This bodily shape, the (beautiful) garments, and the boundless beauty (of bodies) — these too are all deceit alone (the Lord-conjuror is showing them to gladden the beings who have come to the show).
False is the body, false are the clothes; false is incomparable beauty.
False is the body, false is the raiment and false is peerless beauty.
The body, the garments, whatever beauty is gathered, boundless — all are of the form of falsehood.
GXWC: Mia = husband, spouse. Bibi = wife, woman. Khap = being consumed, being engrossed. Khar = ruined, disgraced, dishonoured.
(Somewhere the Lord has made) men (and somewhere) women; all these too are of the form of deceit, who, engrossed (in this deceit in the form of the bond of woman and man), are being ruined.
False is the husband, false is the wife; they mourn and waste away.
False is husband and false is wife, who pine away and become miserable.

Husband and wife — the whole show is false. 'Kur' is to be taken with all the words; taking this to be true and clinging to it, being consumed and consumed, the beings become (khar) destroyed; or they become ruined, or they become miserable, or (khar) they become ashes.
S373: Kur = in the deceit, in the delusion. Kurai = of the deceitful person, of the being caught in the delusion.
The being caught in this (visible) deceit has fallen in love with the deceit, and because of this he has forgotten his own Creator.
The false ones love falsehood, and forget their Creator.
The false one loves what is false and forgets the Creator.
Those false ones whose love has become fixed on these false things — the Being has been forgotten by them.
C65Y: (It does not remain in his memory that) the whole world is perishable, and one should not fix attachment on anyone at all.
With whom should I become friends, if all the world shall pass away?
With whom should I contract friendship the whole world is to pass away.
Therefore with which of the things of Maya shall we make friendship? The whole world is (chalanhar) perishable.
N8SL: Mitha = tasty, dear. Pur = (life is a boat, all beings are its 'pur'); all the beings.
(This whole world is deceit, but this) deceit seems dear (to all beings), it tastes sweet (as) honey; in this way this deceit is drowning all the beings.
False is sweetness, false is honey; through falsehood, boat-loads of men have drowned.
False is sweetness and false is honey. In falsehood the boat loads are drowned.
Falsehood (mitha) is like arsenic, yet falsehood is perceived after the manner of (makhio) honey. This falsehood has drowned boatload upon boatload in the world.
Z22J: Nanak vakhanai = Nanak says. Kuro kur = deceit upon deceit, delusion upon delusion. ❀ Note: in this salok the words 'kur', 'kur' (locative) and 'kurai' are all three worth understanding. 'Kuru' is a noun, nominative case, singular. The form 'kur' is the locative singular of 'kuru'. The word 'kurai' is the genitive singular of 'kura'. It needs to be borne in mind that the word 'kurai' is from 'kura', not from 'kuru'. The word 'kura' is the Prakrit and Punjabi form of the Sanskrit word kutak, which is an adjective and whose meaning is 'false, caught in delusion'. ||1||
(O Lord!) Nanak makes his plea (before You) that without You (this world) is deceit. ||1||
Nanak speaks this prayer: without You, Lord, everything is totally false. ||1||
Nanak, makes a supplication except You, O my Master, everything is thoroughly false.

Sri Guru Ji says: O Vahiguru! Without Your Name all is falsehood upon falsehood. Therefore I make this very plea, that You give me Your own true Name. ||1|| ☬ If it be said: in this world of the form of falsehood, how is truth to be obtained? Upon that, from His own mouth, he speaks these words:
N6C9: Ta par = only then, at that time alone. Janiai = it can be known. Sach = (the opposite of the word 'kur' is the word 'sach'; the meaning of 'kur' is 'deceit', which is without reality, which exists only as long as its maker wishes its existence. Against this, the meaning of 'sach' is) reality. Ridai = in the heart. Sacha = the possessor of reality, Hari.
(Turning desire away from the deceit in the form of the world, the understanding of the world's) reality comes only then, when that Master of reality (God) settles within a person's heart.
One knows the Truth only when the Truth is in his heart.
Then alone the man is known as true, if the truth be in his heart.
Then (par) truth is well known, when a person becomes true in his heart.
SPFC: Kur ki mal = the filth of the deceit in the form of Maya (upon the mind).

Then the effect of Maya's deceit is removed from the mind (then, along with the mind, the body too becomes beautiful, the bodily senses also turn away from the foul side; as it were) the body is washed clean.
The filth of falsehood departs, and the body is washed clean.
His filth of falsehood departs and he washed his body clean.
Let the filth of falsehood be removed, and let one wash and purify the body by the remembrance of the Name.
060V: (The risings of the mind ceasing towards Maya's deceit, the understanding of the) reality (of nature) comes only then, when a person joins his mind to that reality,
One knows the Truth only when he bears love to the True Lord.
Then alone, man is known as true, if he bears love to the True One.
Truth is then well known, when one holds love for the true Vahiguru.
DFZH: Rahsiai = it blossoms. Mokh duar = the door of liberation, the way of release from the chains of the deceit in the form of Maya.
(Then), hearing the Name (of that Possessor of reality) a person's mind blossoms, and he finds the way to become free (of the bonds of Maya).
Hearing the Name, the mind is enraptured; then, he attains the gate of salvation.
When the mind is enraptured on hearing the Name, then the mortal obtains the door of salvation.
Hearing (sun) the true Name, let one (man) reflect on it, let one (rahsiai) contemplate it deeply; then (mokh duar) knowledge is obtained.
LPS3: Jugat = the way of passing one's life in a fine manner.
The understanding of the Lord, the world's reality, comes then, when a person knows the way (of passing) a godly life,
One knows the Truth only when he knows the true way of life.
Then alone is the man deemed to be true, if the knows the true way of life.
Truth is well known when the being knows the (jugat) joining of his attention upon Vahiguru.
ZLSC: Dharat kaia = the earth in the form of the body. Dei = let him give, let him sow. Karta biu = the seed (in the form of the 'Name') of the Kartar.
that is, having prepared the earth in the form of the body, let him sow the Lord's Name in it.
Preparing the field of the body, he plants the Seed of the Creator.
Preparing the body field, he puts into it the seed of the Creator.
Having purified the earth of the body by desireless deeds, let him give — that is, put in — the seed of the Kartar's Name.
5ZT8: The testing of truth comes then, when one takes the true teaching (from the Guru),
One knows the Truth only when he receives true instruction.
Then alone is the mortal deemed to be true when he receives the true instruction.
Truth is well known when one (lei) holds to the true teaching.
1MX9: and (walking upon that teaching) learns the way of showing mercy to all beings and does some charity and giving (to the needy).
Showing mercy to other beings, he makes donations to charities.
He shows mercy to living beings and gives something in charity.

Let him show mercy for the sake of the liberation of his own soul — that is, for release from wandering through the eighty-four — or, casting the glance of mercy upon all beings, (janai) knowing, let him do what he can; (dan) let him give with the proper rite, taking water and kusa grass, with the materials of merit. This is what is called punn dan; or, to give at a meritorious time, that is punn dan.
SK7J: Atam tirath = at the pilgrimage place in the form of the soul.
Acquaintance with that innermost reality comes only then, when a person settles at the innermost pilgrimage place,
One knows the Truth only when he dwells in the sacred shrine of pilgrimage of his own soul.
Then alone is one knows as true, when he abides in the pilgrimage station of his heart.
Truth is then well known, when the mind takes its dwelling at the pilgrimage place of the soul. ☬ How is he to do it?
ZLZQ: Bah rahai = let him remain seated, let him hold the mind back from running towards vices.
having taken the teaching from his own Guru, let him remain seated at that inner pilgrimage place; let him keep his dwelling there always.
He sits and receives instruction from the True Guru, and lives in accordance with His Will.
He takes instruction from the Guru and sits and abides according to his will.

Having asked of the Satgurus, being settled, let him remain seated in Him who is dwelling within all — that is, let him remain unwavering. Or (bah rahai) the sense is in the mastering of the posture, and let him make the mind free of craving.
3V6J: He Himself becomes the cure of all the sufferings of those people, (because He) washes out and removes all the vices (from that heart where He is dwelling),
Truth is the medicine for all; it removes and washes away our sins.
Truth is the medicine for all and it removes and washed away the sin.
Truth, that which is, has become the medicine of all diseases. Washing the filth in the form of sins, it drives it out from within the mind.
ZBV9: Nanak makes his plea — those within whose hearts the Lord, the Master of reality, is settled. ||2||
Nanak speaks this prayer to those who have Truth in their laps. ||2||
Nanak makes supplication to those, who have truth in their lap.
Sri Guru Ji says: those in whose (palai) garment, or lap — that is, in whose heart — there is the true Name: if the being makes his plea before them, then he obtains liberation. ||2||
ZUXC: Dan = bounty. Mahinda = mine, that is, for me. Tali khak = the dust of the soles (of the feet), the dust of the feet. Ta = then.
(My mind desires this, that I be given) the bounty of the dust of the feet (of the saints). If this bounty be obtained, then it should be applied to the forehead.
The gift I seek is the dust of the feet of the Saints; if I were to obtain it, I would apply it to my forehead.
For me gift it the dust of saints feet. If I obtain it, then, I shall apply it to my forehead.
(Mahinda) my bounty is the dust of the soles of the feet of the saints; if it be obtained, then let it be applied to the forehead.
H0QY: Kura = that which entangles one in deceit, that which entangles one in the net of Maya. Alakh = the unseen.
(Other) greed, which entangles one only in the net of Maya, should be abandoned, and joining the mind to the Lord alone one should perform His devotion,
Renounce false greed, and meditate single-mindedly on the unseen Lord.
Forsake false avarice and with single mind meditate you on the Unseen Lord.
Let us abandon false greed, and becoming of one mind let us meditate on the unseen Being.
11D2: Teveho = of just that kind. Jevehi = of whatever kind.
(because) whatever kind of work a person does, of just that kind is the fruit he obtains.
As are the actions we commit, so are the rewards we receive.
As are the deeds, we do, so is the fruit which we obtain.
As is the work one does, (teveho) of that kind is the fruit obtained.
XX3L: Purab = from before, from the beginning, from the very first. Likhia = the presence of the impressions of the deeds done in the past.
But the dust of the feet of the saintly people is obtained only if one's fortune is good.
If it is so pre-ordained, then one obtains the dust of the feet of the Saints.
If it is so writ in the beginning, then, the man obtains the dust of the feet of those Saints.
If, according to former deeds, a good writ has been written, then the dust of the feet of those saints is obtained.
6B9M: Mat thori = if one's own understanding be small, if one keeps the support of one's own small understanding. ||10||
(Abandoning the support and reliance of the gurmukhs,) if one keeps the support of one's own shallow understanding, then the labour performed (on that support) goes in vain. ||10||
But through small-mindedness, we forfeit the merits of selfless service. ||10||
For reasons of meager intellect we lose the value of service.
By doing the service of the saints let us lose our petty understanding; or, by having small understanding the service is lost.
SKRK: Sach = in truth. Sach kal = a famine has fallen upon truth, the discernment of reality has not remained. Kalakh = blackness, the soot of vices. Betal = a ghost, a spectre.

(From the hearts of worldly beings) truth has flown away and deceit upon deceit is holding sway; because of the soot (of the sins) of Kaljug the beings are becoming ghosts (that is, attachment to the world is growing strong, the thought of forming a bond with the Maker of the world is going far from the hearts of the beings, and without remembrance the beings are, as it were, ghosts).
There is a famine of Truth; falsehood prevails, and the blackness of the Dark Age of Kali Yuga has turned men into demons.
There is a famine of truth, falsehood prevails and the blackness of the Dark age has made men demons.
In Kaljug, through the soot of sins, all the beings are becoming (betal) ghosts; a famine of the speaking of truth has fallen, and falsehood is prevailing among all.
03QU: Biu = the seed in the form of the Name. Bij = having sown. Kiu ugvai = it cannot sprout. Dal = the two halves of the grain, separated.

Those who sowed the seed (of Hari's Name in their hearts) went from this world having earned honour. But now the sprouting (of the Name) has ceased, (because the minds) are like a split pulse (they are in two halves — that is, because of double-mindedness the beings' minds do not join to the Name).
Those who planted their seed have departed with honor; now, how can the shattered seed sprout?
They, who have sown the seed of the Name have departed with honour. How can the broken seed sprout now?

Those who in the former age sowed the seed of the deeds of sacrifice and the rest went, taking honour, into the heavens and the rest. Now in this age that seed has become a split pulse — that is, neither have the rishis remained, nor has the wealth remained, nor has power remained in the mantras. Now those who wish to do those deeds, that they should (ugvai) sprout — they never will.
NG90: Ik = a whole seed. Ruti hu rut = the season among seasons, that is, a good season, a fitting season. Pah = the mordant, that which is put into the water before the dye in order to make the colour fast upon the cloth.

The seed sprouts only if the seed is whole and the season of sowing is also good and fitting (in the same way, God's Name-sprout too shoots up only if the mind is whole, if it stays turned wholly towards God, and if the time, the ambrosial hour, is also not let slip).
If the seed is whole, and it is the proper season, then the seed will sprout.
if the seed be whole and there be the proper season, then the seed germinates.

If there be one grain — that is, if the full materials of the sacrifice be there — and if there be the season among seasons, that is, if it be Sat, Treta or Duapur, then (ugvai) it will spring up, that is, the deed will be a giver of fruit.
4JYA: Korai = to the unbleached (cloth). Rang soi = that (fast) colour which (ought to be, that is) a fine fast colour.
O Nanak! If the mordant is not applied, then the unbleached cloth does not take that (fine fast) colour (which it takes when the mordant is applied).
O Nanak, without treatment, the raw fabric cannot be dyed.
Nanak, without a mordant, the brand new cloth cannot be dyed.

Sri Guru Ji says: just as without the giving of the mordant there is no (soi) beauty of colour upon unbleached cloth, so here there is no beauty of the deeds and no proper fruit comes of them. ☬ He now gives the illustration of cloth for the materials:
7ZD9: Saram = labour. Rapai = let it be dyed.

(In the same way, if this unbleached mind is to be given a fine colour in the dye of God's Name, then first) let us put it on the bleaching-ground of God's fear; then let us give it the mordant of labour and effort.
In the Fear of God it is bleached white, if the treatment of modesty is applied to the cloth of the body.
If the mordant of modesty be modesty be applied to the body it is washed white of sins in Lord's fear.

To remain in the fear of Vahiguru — let the cloth of the mind be put upon this bleaching-ground; to feel (saram) shame at evil deeds — let this be the mordant to (tan) the body, that is, to the subtle body, the mind.
SMVU: Kurai = of deceit, of trickery and cheating. Soi = news, a whisper. ||1||
(After this) O Nanak! If (this mind) be dyed in God's devotion, then the deceit of Maya cannot even come near it. ||1||
O Nanak, if one is imbued with devotional worship, his reputation is not false. ||1||
Nanak, if the man be imbed with the Lord's meditation, then, his repute is not false even in the least.
Sri Guru Ji says: if it be (rapai) dyed in the madder-dye in the form of devotion, then not even (soi) a trace of the mind's falsehood remains. ||1|| ☬ He describes the rule of Kaljug:
5CC6: Lab = the craving of the tongue. Mahta = the vizier. Sikdar = the headman.
(In the world, for the beings) the craving of the tongue is, as it were, the king; sin is the vizier; and falsehood is the headman,
Greed and sin are the king and prime minister; falsehood is the treasurer.
Both avarice and sin are the King and Minister and falsehood is the Master of Mint.
Greed is the king; (mahta) the vizier, or the record-keeper, is sin; falsehood has been made (sikdar) the police officer, or the chief.
Gluttony/greed and sin are like the king and minister, and falsehood is the chief. Lust is the deputy whom they consult and summon, and acts as their chief advisor.
10Y9: Neb = the deputy. Sad = having called, having summoned.
(In this very court of greed and sin) lust is the deputy; summoning him, his advice is asked; he alone is their great counsellor.
Sexual desire, the chief advisor, is summoned and consulted; they all sit together and contemplate their plans.
Lust, the assistant official, is summoned and consulted and they all sit together and chalk out evil plans.

Lust is (neb) the mace-bearer; calling him, his advice is asked. Sitting and sitting, all four hold counsel among themselves about sin; the sense being that in Kaljug the kings are greedy, and the viziers or record-keepers are sinful, the chiefs are false and the mace-bearers lustful — then from where should justice be got?

7FZL: Andhi rayat = the beings blinded by remaining subject to lust and the other vices. Bhah = fire, the fire of craving. Murdar = what is forbidden, a bribe, graft. Bhare murdar = (the subjects) pay the levy.
(Their) subjects, being void of knowledge, are as it were blinded, and are paying the levy of the fire of craving.
Their subjects are blind, and without wisdom, they try to please the will of the dead.
The subjects are blind and, without wisdom, they satisfy the Official's fire or greed with bribe carrion.
These subjects are blind, being void of the knowledge of dharam and adharam. The beings, filled with the (bhah) fire in the form of craving, eat (murdar) what is another's right.
The subjects (our senses and mind) are blinded by these vices and lack wisdom; they pay the price of their fire of desire,
VC4F: Giani = those who give teaching to others. Vaveh = they play. Rup kareh = they change into many guises.
Those people who have themselves called men of knowledge (preachers) dance, play instruments, and change into many guises and make ornament of themselves;
The spiritually wise dance and play their musical instruments, adorning themselves with beautiful decorations.
The divines dance, play musical instruments and disguise and decorate themselves.

Those who are (giani) knowers of the doings of Krishna Ji dance, and before them they play the instruments. Adorning themselves with garments and ornaments they make up the form of Krishna and Radhika; the sense being this, that in order to fill their own bellies they play the buffoon by mimicking their own elders.
The 'gyanis' are dancing and playing their instruments, and wear various costumes (re-enacting plays of spiritual tales). These 'learned' people shout loudly and sing war epics (poems) of warriors.
YGP6: Vada = the episodes of quarrels and wars. Jodha ka vichar = the exposition of the tales of heroes.
Those men of knowledge cry out loudly, recite the episodes of wars, and expound the ballads of the heroes.
They shout out loud, and sing epic poems and heroic stories.
They shout aloud and sing of epic poems and heroes tales.
And in a high pitch they (kukeh) shout out cries. So, having considered, they sing (vada) the useless (vad) contention, and they make their exposition of (jodha) the heroes alone.
JRA9: Hikmat = cleverness. Hujat = argument. Sanjai = in the gathering of Maya.
The learned fools know only how to practise cleverness and to give arguments, (but) they are joined together in the gathering of Maya.
The fools call themselves spiritual scholars, and by their clever tricks, they love to gather wealth.
The fools call themselves scholars and with devices and cavils, they love to amass wealth.
Those who, having learnt (hikmat) cleverness, practise (hujat) idle disputation, and through that make their love the (sanjai) gathering of wealth — those who are fools are called the pandits of Kal.

The foolish pandits use their cleverness to win arguments but are engrossed/in love with accumulating wealth. Those who call themselves righteous (i.e. religious) waste their righteousness by begging for liberation (and in doing so, are treating God like a genie, and are righteous for the sake of a reward rather than true love and devotion).
67AD: Dharmi = those who consider themselves to be men of dharam. Gavaveh = they lose. Mokh duar = the door of liberation.

(Those people who) consider themselves men of dharam do, for their own part, the work of dharam, but they lose (all their labour), (because in exchange for it) they ask for the door of liberation, that we may be liberated (that is, they do the work of dharam but not desirelessly; they are still bound by craving).
The righteous waste their righteousness, by asking for the door of salvation.
The virtuous disfigure their meritorious acts by asking for the door of salvation.

Those who are the men of dharam of Kaljug lose dharam by doing dharam; then they ask for knowledge, the door of liberation, or they ask for liberation at the door — the sense being that having done a good deed they want the fruit at that very moment.
0YQK: Jati = those people who have kept their senses under control. Jugat = the way (of becoming a jati). Chhad baheh = they abandon. Ghar bar = household, house and home.
(There are many such who) have themselves called jatis; they do not know the way of being a jati, (and merely following others) they leave house and home.
They call themselves celibate, and abandon their homes, but they do not know the true way of life.
