Those who in Kaljug are called (jati) sannyasis do not know the way of renunciation; leaving the house they go and sit in (bar) the waste. In just this much they hold themselves to be jatis. Or, they abandon house and home. On the way of sannyas, the authority of the Tenth Guru Ji: ☬ 'O mind, practise such renunciation: ☬ understand the forest and the house to be all alike, and be detached within the mind itself.'

The celibates do not truly know the way of celibacy and the right way to live as they abandon their homes (where they could learn to control their senses and help others in their lives). Such is the extent of peoples sins that everyone thinks they are perfect, and nobody considers themselves lowly or imperfect.
WRMM: Sabh ko = every being. Pura = complete, unerring. Ghat = deficient.
(Such is the sway of this greed, sin, falsehood and lust that) (wherever you look) every being considers himself completely wise. No person says that there is any deficiency in him.
Everyone calls himself perfect; none call themselves imperfect.
Everyone deems himself perfect and none call himself imperfect.
Everyone sits taking himself to be complete in qualities; no one calls himself deficient.
SKD9: Pat = honour. Parvana = the weight. Pichhai = in the far pan (of the scales). ||2||

But O Nanak! A person turns out full in the weighing (that is, in the testing) only if in the other pan of the scales the weight in the form of the honour (received in God's court) is placed; the sense being that he alone is free of deficiency who receives honour in the Lord's court. ||2||
If the weight of honor is placed on the scale, then, O Nanak, one sees his true weight. ||2||
If the weight of honour be put into the hind scale, then alone, O Nanak, the man appears properly weighed.

Sri Guru Ji says: but when the (parvana) weight in the form of honour is placed in the far pan — those qualities by which the honour of the great souls has come down: let that weight in the form of qualities be placed in the far pan of the scales in the form of the understanding, that is, let the qualities of the great souls of the past be set on one side and considered in the understanding, and on the other side let one's own qualities be placed, that is, considered — then, having been weighed, it (japai) is known whether he is equal to them or less. ||2||
When in God's court, and our honour is weighed (assessed), then (Nanak) we will see our true value.
9SQP: Vadi = fixed, appointed by God. Su = that very thing. Vajag = it will sound, it will become manifest. Sacha = the ever-abiding Lord. Vekhai = He is caring for (every being).
O Nanak! Whatever thing has been settled by God, that alone will come to pass, (because) that true Lord is (Himself) caring for (every being).
Evil actions become publicly known; O Nanak, the True Lord sees everything.
Wickedness becomes well known, but He, the True Lord sees everything, O Nanak.
Sri Guru Ji says: what Parmeshvar has (vadi) framed and fashioned, (su vajag) that becomes manifest; and that True One is watching everything — nothing is hidden from Him.

Whatever God decides for us will come to pass, Nanak; the True Lord watches over everything. Everyone tries their best (jumps around using their own strength), but only what the Creator does actually happens.
XWHT: Sabhni = all the beings. Chhala marian = they have applied their own force. Su hoi = that alone comes to pass.
All the beings apply their own force each in his own way, but that alone happens which the Kartar does.
Everyone makes the attempt, but that alone happens which the Creator Lord does.
Every one has taken a jump, but what the Creator does, that alone comes to pass.
However many beings there are, all have made their leaps — that is, they have performed their disciplines; but he whom the Creator Being approves, he alone is accomplished by those disciplines.
SGQW: Agai = there, where one has to go after leaving this body. Jat = that is, the distinction of any high or low caste. Jor = force.

In God's court there is no (distinction of high or low) caste, nor can anyone's force prevail, because there one deals with beings who are strangers (that is, they know nothing of anyone's high caste or force, and therefore come under no pressure).
In the world hereafter, social status and power mean nothing; hereafter, the soul is new.
In the next world, caste and power count not; hereafter, the mortal has to deal with the new beings.

There, in the world beyond, there is neither caste nor strength. There the beings are new — that is, the people are strangers; or, those people will not address you with 'jiu'. They will address you with the low address of 've' and 're'.
In the next world, power and social caste do not matter; there is a new order of life (merit-based). In God's assessment, only those few whose actions pleased God are honoured.
67CM: Sei kei = those few (beings) alone. Lekhai = at the time of the reckoning. ||3||

There only those few people are counted good who receive honour at the time of the reckoning of deeds (that is, those who had done good deeds in the world, and who therefore receive honour at God's door). ||3||
Those few, whose honor is confirmed, are good. ||3||
A few, whose honour is of account, they are good.
Those few alone will be good whose honour will fall into the reckoning there — that is, will be approved. ||3||
HU5Y: Dhur = from the beginning, from the first. Karam = bounty, mercy.
(O Lord!) Those people upon whom You have bestowed Your bounty from the very first, they alone have remembered the Master (that is, You).
Only those whose karma You have pre-ordained from the very beginning, O Lord, meditate on You.
Only they, whose destiny You, O Lord, have so written from the beginning, meditate on you.
O Akal Purakh! Those upon whom You from the beginning have placed Your karam — that is, have shown mercy — they have meditated on (khasam) the Master, that is, on You.
Only those who You have blessed have the ability to meditate on You (i.e. not our greatness, but God's mercy). On our own, we have nothing and You have created the various beings of the world.
5S1H: Tudh = You, O Kartar! Veki = of many kinds, of many colours.
These beings have nothing in their own power (that they might remember You). You have created a world of many colours;
Nothing is in the power of these beings; You created the various worlds.
Nothing is in the power of these creatures. You have created the diverse worlds.
(Tudh veki) You have brought forth a world of separate and separate kinds, that is, of many sorts. Therefore in these beings' own power there is nothing.
8J6H: Ikna no = to many beings. Ik = many beings. Apahu = from Your own self. Tudh = You, O Lord! Khuaia = they are led astray, they are put aside.
Many beings You keep joined to Your own feet, but many beings You have kept separated from Yourself.
Some, You unite with Yourself, and some, You lead astray.
Some You unitest with Yourself and some you leadest astray from You.
Some You show mercy and join to Yourself; some You have (khuaia) made to forget Your own form.

Some You unite with Yourself, and others You have led astray from You. Through the Guru's Grace, You are known, wherever You choose to reveal Yourself. Those people merge naturally into the Truth. ||11||
V9D7: Jania = has come to know (You). Jithai = within which person. Ap = one's own self. Bujhaia = has made to understand.
That (very fortunate) person within whose heart You have placed the understanding of Your own self, he by the Satguru's grace has recognised You,
By Guru's Grace You are known; through Him, You reveal Yourself.
You are known by the grace of the Guru, through whom You revealest yourself.
By the grace of the Gurus You have been known there, (jithai) in that heart where You Yourself, being pleased, have given understanding to the seekers, that is, have given knowledge.
T8YM: Sahje hi = of itself. Sach = in truth, in steadiness, in stillness, in reality. Samaia = becomes absorbed. ||11||
and he has of himself become one with (his own) reality. ||11||
We are easily absorbed in You. ||11||
They are easily absorbed in the True Lord.
He to whom He has given understanding, he naturally — O Truth-form! — has become absorbed in You.
LHJ7: (O Lord! Your kudrat is wondrous, that) affliction becomes the cure (of the beings' diseases), and comfort becomes (for them) the cause of suffering. But if (true spiritual) comfort be obtained (by a being), then (suffering) does not remain.
Suffering is the medicine, and pleasure the disease, because where there is pleasure, there is no desire for God.
Pain is the medicine and pleasure the malady, and where there is pleasure, there is no desire for God.

The comfort of the senses has become the disease, and the suffering of jap and tap has become the medicine. When there is the comfort of the senses, then there is no (tam) desire at all for attaining the Lord, that is, for doing jap and tap. The sense being: the suffering of birth and death is the disease, and for its removal the Name of the comfort-form Parmeshvar is the medicine. When the being obtains the medicine of the Name in the form of comfort, then what disease, what suffering in the form of birth and death, will come to that person again? It does not.

Suffering is the medicine, pleasure the disease — where there is pleasure/comfort, there is no longing for God. You are the Creator-Doer, I am nothing; if I consider myself to be something (if I say "I"), it is not appropriate. I am a sacrifice to You, who resides in His creation. Your limits cannot be comprehended. In Your creation is Your light, in Your light is creation; You pervade everywhere, filling all. You are the eternal, stable Lord, Your praises are beautiful — whoever has sung Your praises has been carried over (the world-ocean of maya).
TYSQ: Karna = the doer. Mai nahi = I am nothing at all, I have no standing. Ja hau kari = if I say 'I', if I take myself to be something. Na hoi = it does not become, this thing does not befit. ||1||

O Lord! You are the Kartar, the doer (You Yourself understand these secrets); I have not the capacity (to understand). If I take myself to be something (that is, if I begin to think that I can understand Your secret) then this thing does not befit. ||1||
You are the Creator Lord; I can do nothing. Even if I try, nothing happens. ||1||
You are the Doer, I can do nothing. Even if I try to do something, it comes to nothing.
You are the Kartar of the form of grace; I can do nothing. Even if I should wish to do something, being dependent it does not come about. ||1||
God, You are the doer and Creator, I am not (i.e. not in my control). Whatever is done is not by my own efforts, but Yours.
2Z0P: O Kartar dwelling within the creation! I am a sacrifice to You,
I am a sacrifice to Your almighty creative power which is pervading everywhere.
Sacrifice am I to You. who abides in His creation.
Having fashioned the world through the kudrat of Maya, and then dwelling within it — I go as a sacrifice to You.
I am a sacrifice to the God who is manifest in the whole universe. I cannot understand Your limits (it is beyond my understanding) . ||1|| Pause ||
QHBC: Your limit cannot be found. ||1|| Rahau ||
Yours limit cannot be comprehended. Pause.
Your limit is not perceived by anyone. ||1|| Rahau ||
3CC1: Jat = the creation. Jot = God's light. Jot mah = within all the lights, within all the beings. Jata = is seen, is appearing. Akal = complete. Kala = a piece, a portion. Akal kala = He of whom there are no separate pieces, the Lord complete and undivided.
Your light alone is dwelling within the whole creation; Your light alone is within all the beings; You are pervading everywhere without break.
Your Light is in Your creatures, and Your creatures are in Your Light; Your almighty power is pervading everywhere.
Your light is contained in the creatures and the creatures are contained in Yours light. You O mighty Inconceivable Lord, are filling all.

O Light! Within You is (jata) the origin, or the castes of brahmin and the rest — that is, the world in its imagined form. And O Light! You are complete within the world in the form of origin, as its substratum. And (akal) free of affliction, You are pervading everywhere through Your own (kala) power.
Your Light is in the Creation, and the Creation is within Your Light. You are both in everyone (divided) but yet One and permeate all.
CABV: Sualiu = fine, beautiful. Jin kiti = he who has done (Your praise).
O Lord! You are ever-abiding; Your praises are beautiful. Whoever has sung Your qualities has crossed over the world-ocean.
You are the True Lord and Master; Your Praise is so beautiful. One who sings it, is carried across.
You are the True Lord, and beautiful is Your praise. He who hymns it, swims across.
You are the true Master; Your praise is (sualiu) beautiful. He who has done Your praise has crossed over the ocean of the world.
K9PD: Nanak = O Nanak! Kahu karte kia bata = speak the words of the Kartar. ||2||
O Nanak! (You too) speak the praise and laudation of the Kartar, (and say that) the Lord is doing whatever He thinks good to do (that is, in His doings no one has any part). ||2||
Nanak speaks the stories of the Creator Lord; whatever He is to do, He does. ||2||
Nanak tells the tales of the Creator that what the Lord is to do, that He continues to do.

Sri Guru Ji says: O Parmeshvar Ji! We speak Your words. Whatever You have to do, You are doing it — the sense being that nothing separate from You is done by the being. ||2|| ☬ He states the answer to the Sikh's six questions:
Says Nanak, praise the Creator, saying that whatever He chooses to do, He does (that is right). ||2||
YX0K: Sabdan = the Guru's word, the Guru's teaching, the Guru's command, the being's dharam. Jog sabdan = the dharam of yoga. Sabdan brahmanah = the dharam of the brahmins.
The dharam of yoga is to obtain knowledge (to reflect on Brahm). The dharam of the brahmins is the reflection on the Veds.
The Way of Yoga is the Way of spiritual wisdom; the Vedas are the Way of the Brahmins.
The way of union with the Lord is the way of Divine Knowledge but with the Brahmans, the way is through the Vedas.

For the sannyasis who (jog) join their attention to Akal Purakh, the reflection on the one Brahm alone is (sabdan) their dharam or teaching. For the brahmins, the reading and teaching of the Ved and the rest — this alone is their dharam or teaching.
The Way (Dharma) of the Yogi is the pursuit of spiritual wisdom (Gyan, typically through meditation/samadhi); the Way of the Brahmin is the study/knowledge of the Vedas.
AMBJ: Parakritah = to do another's labour, to serve others.

The Way of the Khshatriya is the Way of bravery; the Way of the Shudras is service to others.
Khatri's way is the way of bravery, of the Sudras the way is the service of others.

For the khatris, valour and the rest alone is the dharam or teaching. (Prakrit) to do farming and such labour well — this is the dharam or teaching of the vaishyas. For the shudras, to do another's labour, to serve, is the dharam or teaching.
The Way of the Khatri is the Way of the Warrior (Bravery); the Way of the Shudra is service to others.
102P: Sarab sabdan = the dharam of all dharams, that is, the highest dharam of all. Ek sabdan = the dharam in the form of the remembrance of the one Lord. Bheu = the secret.
But the chief dharam of all is this, that we remember the one Lord. The person who knows this secret,
The Way of all is the Way of the One; Nanak is a slave to one who knows this secret;
If any one knows the secret, the duty of all is one Lord's meditation.
The common dharam or teaching of all is this: to know the one non-dual Brahm. Whoever knows this secret —
But the Way of all ways (the supreme duty for all) is only One (God). Whoever understands this mystery...
6N8Y: Soi = that very person. Niranjan deu = is (the form of) the Lord. ||3||
Nanak is his slave; that person is the form of the Lord. ||3||

Nanak is a servant of him who understands this as he himself is the immaculate Lord.

The one Parmatma alone is the soul of all the gods; He is the soul of the gods of the gods also.
The One Lord Krishna is the Divine Lord of all; He is the Divinity of the individual soul.

(Kris) they call being, which is the referent of the word 'tat'; (nan) is in the sense of bliss. The one who is the god Krishna, He is the illuminating god of all the gods; He alone, Ishvar, is (atma) of the form of the being.
The One Lord is the Soul of all gods, and the Soul of the gods of gods.
092B: Vasdev = (just as the meaning of the word 'Krishna' is also 'Parmatma', so this name of Krishna Ji too is to be taken only in the sense of 'Parmatma') Parmatma. Basudevasyi = of Parmatma. Basudevasyi atma = the soul of the Lord.
The person who comes to know the secret of the Lord's soul,
Nanak is a slave to anyone who understands this mystery of the all-pervading Lord;
If any one knows the mystery of the soul and the Omnipresent Lord,
(Atma) the being is the form of (Vasudev) Brahm; whoever knows this secret —
ENTD: Niranjan = Hari, free of anjan (that is, of the soot in the form of Maya). ||4||
Nanak is that person's slave; he is the form of Parmatma. ||4||
He himself is the Immaculate Divine Lord. ||4||
of him Nanak, is a slave as he himself is the Pure Lord.

...Nanak is a slave to him; that person who realises that God is beyond Maya (and knows the reality of God) ||4||
UEJL: Kumbh = a pot. Kumbhe = within the pot alone. Badha = is bound. Rahai = remains, can stay. Kumbh na hoi = the pot does not come about, the pot cannot be made.

Water remains confined within the pitcher, but without water, the pitcher could not have been formed;
As the water remains confined in a pitcher, but the pitcher cannot be shaped without water,
Without (kumbhe) the pot the water is not still; without water and the potter the pot cannot be made.

Just as a jug/pitcher holds water, but without water, the pitcher itself cannot be formed; similarly, the mind remains stable only when bound by spiritual wisdom, and without the Guru, this wisdom cannot be found.
AQXM: (so) the mind can stay settled (in one place) only when bound by the (Guru's) knowledge (that is, teaching), (that is, it does not run towards vices), and without the Guru knowledge cannot arise. ||5||
just so, the mind is restrained by spiritual wisdom, but without the Guru, there is no spiritual wisdom. ||5||
so the mind, controlled by Divine knowledge is restrained, but sans the Guru, there can be no gnosis.

B47Z: Parhia = a person who has read. Gunahgar = one who does evil deeds. Omi = one who knows only the word 'om', that is, an unlettered person. Sadh = a good person. Na mariai = he does not take a beating.

If a lettered person becomes a doer of evil (then seeing this the unlettered person should not be dismayed, thinking that if this is the state of the lettered, what will become of the unlettered; because if) the unlettered person is good then he does not take a beating. if an educated person is the sinner, then an illiterate saints is not to be punished (because of his illiteracy).

If an educated person becomes an evildoer (then seeing this, an illiterate person should not panic thinking "if this is the state of the educated, what will happen to the illiterate?", because if) the illiterate person is righteous, then he is not punished. (The judgment is based on the person's earnings/actions; reading or not reading has no value).
JRBV: Ghalna ghale = let him do the labour. Teveho = of just that kind. Pachariai = becomes current, becomes renowned.
Whatever kind of deed a person does, of just that kind does his name become renowned;
As are the deeds done, so is the reputation one acquires.
As are the deeds a man does, so is the Name, he acquires.

Whatever kind of actions a human performs, exactly that kind of name becomes prominent (known) for him.
ULJM: Kala = a game. Jit = because of which.
(Therefore) one should not play such a game as makes one lose the wager (of human birth) on going to the court.

Play not such a game, which may bring you defeat on arriving at God's court.

WJSN: Vichariai = it is considered, it is accepted.
Whether a person be lettered or unlettered, in the Lord's court only the reflection on the Lord's qualities is accepted.

Of the educated and the uneducated the accounts shall be adjudged, hereafter.

O brother! The reflection of the lettered and of (omia) the unlettered will be considered hereafter. That is to say, he who receives honour in the world beyond will be called lettered; he who takes the buffets will be called unlettered.
Whether a human is educated or illiterate, in God's Court, only the contemplation of God's virtues is accepted.

The person who walks (in this world) according to his own will alone takes a beating on going ahead. ||12||
One who stubbornly follows his own mind shall suffer in the world hereafter. ||12||
The head strong shall be thrashed in the next World.

Those beings who walk by the mouth of the senses, plundered by them, or the greedy, or the self-willed who babble whatever comes to the mouth — they will be beaten in the world beyond, that is, they will go into hell. The human who walks according to his own will (in this world), he receives punishment ahead (in the next world). ||12||

WVMZ: Meru = just as all the planets (stars) revolve about mount 'Meru', it is the centre of all the 'islands' and gold and diamonds are found in it; just as among the 108 beads of the rosary the chief bead is the 'meru'; just as the chief pearl of a pearl necklace is called 'meru' — so among the countless births of the Lord's creation the chief birth, the human birth, is called 'meru', and the human body is the 'meru' among the bodies of all the other births. Meru sarir ka = of the meru body (among bodies), of the meru body (among the bodies of all the births), of the chief body, that is, for the human body. Rathvah = the one who drives the chariot.

O Nanak! The human body, chief among the eighty-four lakh births, has one chariot and one charioteer (that is, this life is a long journey and the person is the traveller; in order to cross this long journey easily the beings, under the influence of the times, are walking according to their own understanding under someone's guidance, are looking to someone's support. But as time passes on, the natures of the beings are changing, and therefore the beings' aim of life, the purpose of life, is also changing; therefore)
O Nanak, the soul of the body has one chariot and one charioteer.
Nanak, the prime human body has one chariot and one charioteer.
The being seated in the chariot of the body, which is like (meru) the chief bead, is one alone; his chariot of the body is also one; and the impeller of the body, the charioteer, is also one alone.
ZELJ: Jug jug = in each age. Jug = one lifetime of this creation is called a 'jug'. The jugs are four in number: Satjug, Treta, Duapar and Kaljug. The lifetime of each jug is in order 1,728,000; 1,596,000; 864,000 and 472,000 years (the years of human beings); all this time taken together makes one 'maha jug'. The lifetime of each jug has gone on decreasing in order. The thought regarding this is that the bodily strength and character of the beings in these ages goes on growing weaker, and therefore the lifetime of the ages too goes on decreasing along with it. Vataiah = they are exchanged, they keep changing. Giani = people of knowledge. Tah = this matter.
In each age this chariot and charioteer keep changing again and again; wise people understand this secret.
In age after age they change; the spiritually wise understand this.
They change after every age and the divines understand this.
Again, in age after age the chariot and the charioteer are changed. This secret the people of knowledge know.
N1D0: In Satjug the chariot of the human body is 'contentment' and the charioteer is 'dharam' (that is, when the aim of life of people is generally 'dharam', then, 'dharam' being the life-purpose, 'contentment' of itself is their conveyance, the nature of 'contentment' is strong within the beings. These beings are, as it were, of Satjug, they are dwelling in Satjug).
In the Golden Age of Sat Yuga, contentment was the chariot and righteousness the charioteer.
In the Gold-age, contentment is the carriage and piety the driver in front.
In Satjug the chariot of the body was of contentment; dharam was the impeller of the chariot — that is, all the beings were of dharam and contented.
X3Y5: In the Treta age the chariot of the human body is 'jat' (continence), and before this chariot in the form of 'jat' the charioteer is 'jor' (that is, when the aim of people's life is chivalry, then of itself 'jat' is their conveyance; within people who love chivalry the urge to remain 'jati' is strongest of all).
In the Silver Age of Traytaa Yuga, celibacy was the chariot and power the charioteer.
